# Python code built from HTTP request data

`qualor:python/code-injection` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-95](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/95.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data that reaches the source argument of `eval()`, `exec()` or `compile()` in a Flask,
Django or FastAPI application. Request data passed only in the globals or locals namespace is not
reported, since it is not run as code.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Whatever reaches `eval()` or `exec()` runs as Python with the rights of the server: a client can
read files and secrets, open network connections or start processes. Removing `__builtins__` from
the namespace does not make untrusted code safe; Python has many ways back to them.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** a list of ids sent by the client is turned into a Python value with `eval()`.

```python
from flask import Flask, jsonify, request

app = Flask(__name__)


@app.route("/report")
def report():
    ids = eval(request.args["ids"])
    return jsonify(count=len(ids))
```

**Compliant:** `ast.literal_eval()` accepts only Python literals (numbers, strings, lists, ...).

```python
import ast

from flask import Flask, jsonify, request

app = Flask(__name__)


@app.route("/report")
def report():
    ids = ast.literal_eval(request.args["ids"])
    return jsonify(count=len(ids))
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- To turn text into data, parse it: `json.loads()` or `ast.literal_eval()`.
- To let users choose between a few actions, pick the code or function from a fixed allow-list
  (a dict of constants).
- If a fixed expression needs request values, keep the expression constant and pass the values in
  the namespace: `eval(EXPR, {"__builtins__": {}}, {"x": value})`.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Flask
- Django
- FastAPI

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A slice is followed when it slices request data in place (`request.args["expr"][:20]`),
  a variable assigned request data, or a view parameter; a slice of a value built from request
  data (`(request.args["q"] + "x")[:50]`), or of a variable assigned again after the request value
  (`q = q.strip()`, also `q = q + request.args["b"]` or a fallback `q = request.form["q"]`), is
  missed.
- An allow-list is recognised only as a lookup in a module-level dict of literals assigned to an
  upper-case name that is never changed, or as a ternary of constants. A membership check
  (`if x not in ALLOWED: return`) and nested tables are not recognised.
- Request sources are recognised by their shape. A Flask route parameter with a converter
  (`<int:n>`) and a Django URL argument made numeric by its converter still count as request data;
  a function whose first parameter is named `request`, in a module that imports Django, is taken
  for a view; a Flask view parameter annotated `int` is not a source.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/python/code/code-injection.py`](../../../rules/python/code/code-injection.py) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/python/code/code-injection.yml`](../../../rules/python/code/code-injection.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
